card.law_is_about: Replacing Bürgergeld with a revised means-tested basic-security system, including stronger obligations and benefit reductions.
card.they_want: Go beyond the government bill and introduce compulsory work, including placements in private businesses.
card.they_claim: A current Bertelsmann survey shows that the majority of Bürgergeld recipients are not interested in being placed in work.
card.the_problem: The matched survey measures recent job-search behaviour in a restricted sample; not searching in four weeks is not a finding of disinterest. Most non-searchers reported health obstacles.

claim_quote.original: ist die Mehrzahl der Bürgergeldempfänger bei uns jedoch gar nicht daran interessiert.
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: the majority of Bürgergeld recipients here are, however, not interested in that at all.

locator.paragraph: last paragraph, penultimate sentence; antecedent is placement in the labour market in the preceding sentence

request_quote.original: die Idee der AfD einer verpflichtenden „Bürgerarbeit“
request_quote.translation_en: Translation of request fragment: the AfD’s idea of compulsory “citizens’ work”
request_quote.note: The complete sentence endorses this idea; the following sentence explicitly requests a broader definition allowing private-sector work placements.

counter_quote.original: ob sie in den letzten vier Wochen vor der Befragung eine Erwerbstätigkeit gesucht hatten.
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: whether they had looked for employment in the four weeks before the survey.

correction: Describe the result as a majority not actively searching in the previous four weeks in the sampled target group. The survey sampled 25–50-year-old long-term recipients who were unemployed or seeking work, excluding single parents and people in socially insured employment. Reportp 14 finds 54.6%had not searched; p 18 reports health reasons among 74%of non-searchers. This result does not measure the share with no interest in taking a job or accepting placement.
effect: Removes the survey-based majority-disinterest premise used to support stronger compulsory-work obligations. The evidence identifies heterogeneous search barriers and cannot alone establish that compulsion addresses recipients’ willingness.
limits: The actual proportion interested in work across all recipients is not established here. Recent non-search can sometimes coexist with disinterest. The author may use uninterested as loose shorthand for observed non-search rather than a separately measured attitude, but explicitly attributes it to the survey. The report recognises incentive problems and ambiguous motivation; its findings do not rule out compulsory-work policies or show that every non-searcher is unable or willing to work. The adjacent quarter citing financial incentives is not separately alleged erroneous: the primary report itself uses similar summary shorthand.
materiality_explanation: Major editorial judgment: converts a behavioural majority into an adverse motivational majority in a central explanation of why ordinary placement will fail and compulsory work is needed. The broader policy proposal also relies on international comparisons and incentives, which are not disproved.
direction_explanation: Describing a majority as uninterested strengthens the author’s explicit request for more coercive activation. Severity is assessed separately from this direction. No intent is inferred.

confidence.text_source_mismatch: high for the operational distinction; matched-report identification is strong inference from timing, commissioner, majority non-search and matching quarter-incentives detail, not a document-level footnote

context_checked: Read all five author pages(official bundle 167–171), including the preceding reference to labour-market placement and the following quarter-incentives sentence. No definition equating interest with four-week search or survey-population qualification appears.

Read primary survey methods(pp 7,11–12), operational definition(pp 13–14), search-time measure(p 17), non-search reasons(p 18), qualitative interpretations(pp 19–25)and conclusions(pp 34–36). The report itself acknowledges ambiguous motives, possible rationalisations and incentive problems; do not flatten this into a finding that motivation never matters.

The p 14 weighted search-incidence figure and p 17 search-hours figures use different questions/sample counts; the publisher’s press-release 57%is not substituted for the report’s 54.6%. This is not treated as an additional author error.
Survey findings are empirical and do not depend on subsequent amendments; exact bills and motion are archived so the target proposal is not confused with the enacted law.

Primary report p 13 explicitly excludes jobcentre-proposed jobs from its operational definition of independent job search. Thus the preceding placement antecedent does not turn the measured independent-search result into a direct measure of receptiveness to placement.
